_comment: ODBC provider -- feature 13 (OWNER-DECISIONS.md Batch 5; feature doc
013-odbc-provider.md ODBC-DEC-01 + ODBC-DEC-02).
ODBC is Tina4's generic escape hatch - connect to anything with an ODBC
driver. That generality is its weakness: no single dialect, no reliable
metadata, no reliable last-insert-id, and (the audit's headline) its query/
CRUD path had NEVER been exercised against a REAL ODBC source in ANY language.
Every ODBC finding was therefore LATENT and the provider shipped unproven.
ODBC-DEC-01 (provision a real source - the single highest-value action). The
lab provisions unixODBC + the PostgreSQL ODBC driver (psqlodbc 16) pointing at
the lab's real PostgreSQL, and this fixture drives the shared write path
(SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) through REAL ODBC in all four frameworks, no
mocks. Provisioning a real source is what converted every latent finding into
a caught bug - and it caught one the audit did not predict: Ruby could not
connect at all with a connection string (see ODBC-CONNECT below).
MEASURED on the lab (Ubuntu 24.04, unixODBC 2.3.12, psqlodbc 16.00, real
PostgreSQL) 2026-08-12, because the four bindings diverge and none of this may
be assumed:
* Python pyodbc 5.3: cursor.primaryKeys(table=) returns the PK columns;
cursor.rowcount is the real affected count when read BEFORE any secondary
query; getinfo(SQL_DBMS_NAME) identifies the DBMS for the driver-aware
last-id.
* PHP PDO_ODBC (php8.3-odbc): exposes NO SQLPrimaryKeys catalog call, so the
PK is read from INFORMATION_SCHEMA (portable across PG/MySQL/MSSQL).
* Ruby ruby-odbc 0.999993: ODBC::Database#primary_keys(table) returns the PK;
ODBC::Database#drvconnect (SQLDriverConnect) is the call that parses a
connection string.
* Node odbc 2.5: connection.primaryKeys(cat,schema,table) returns the PK;
connection.query() result carries a real .count for DML.
ODBC-CONNECT (Ruby, surfaced only by the real run). Tina4's OdbcDriver.connect
did ODBC::Database.new(connString), which routes to SQLConnect - and SQLConnect
takes a DSN NAME, not a connection string. A DRIVER={...}/DSN=... string (what
Tina4's odbc:/// URL produces) raised '[unixODBC][Driver Manager]Invalid string
or buffer length'. The Ruby ODBC adapter could NEVER connect with a connection
string until now; connect() uses #drvconnect (SQLDriverConnect) instead.
PHP had the mirror gap in its factory: Database::create('odbc:///...') tried to
parse_url() a raw ODBC string (braces/spaces/semicolons) and failed 'Cannot
determine database type' - odbc is now special-cased before the URL parser, so
the documented public surface Database('odbc://...') actually instantiates.
ODBC-PK-STUB (ODBC-DEC-02, UNIVERSAL). get_columns()/columns()/getColumns()
hardcoded primary_key=false in ALL FOUR - the same defect the SQL adapters
fixed. Feature 4's filterless-write guard reads primary_key, so a PK-keyed
update(table, data) with no explicit filter could not introspect the key and
threw. Each adapter now reads the REAL PK: Python/Ruby/Node via the ODBC
catalog (SQLPrimaryKeys), PHP via INFORMATION_SCHEMA (PDO_ODBC has no catalog
call). Mutation-proved: revert to the false stub -> the PK-keyed + non-id-PK
update cases throw the write-guard error, RED (Python 2, PHP 2, Ruby 2, Node 2).
ODBC-PY-QUIRKS (ODBC-DEC-02, Python). execute() ran 'SELECT @@IDENTITY AS id'
after EVERY statement - a SQL-Server-ism baked into a GENERIC adapter. On a
non-SQL-Server source it errored (swallowed) AND, because it ran on the same
cursor, overwrote the INSERT's rowcount to -1 (MEASURED on real PostgreSQL:
insert().affected_rows == -1 with the old code, 1 with the fix). Last-id is now
driver-aware: @@IDENTITY is attempted ONLY after an INSERT and ONLY when
SQL_DBMS_NAME is SQL Server; every other target returns None. And connect()
now HONOURS the username/password params it ignored (appended as UID/PWD).
Mutation-proved: restore the true-original execute() -> affected_rows -1, the
insert case RED; drop the credential append -> the credentials case RED
(the no-UID/PWD scram connection is rejected).
ODBC-NODE-QUIRKS (ODBC-DEC-02, Node). (a) updateAsync() had NO string-WHERE
branch, so a string filter ('id <= ?') was walked with Object.keys -> ['0',
'1',...], building a nonsense WHERE (the exact bug pg/mysql/mssql guard against)
and params was dropped entirely; it now has the string branch + binds params.
(b) executeManyAsync() had NO transaction owns-guard, so nested in a caller's
transaction its commit() committed the OUTER transaction early; it now owns the
transaction only when not already inside one (mirrors pg/mysql/mssql + the
Python master). insertAsync also now routes a batch (array of rows) through
executeManyAsync, so the owns-guard is reachable through db.insert. Credentials
flow through the factory to the adapter too. Mutation-proved: neuter the string
branch -> the string-where case RED (odbc parameter error); force owns=true ->
the owns-guard case RED (3 rows survive the rollback).
ODBC-FAILLOUD (ODBC-DEC-02, PHP). fetch()/fetchOne() SWALLOWED a query error to
an empty result while execute() raised - a real query error hidden as 'no rows',
contrary to the framework's fail-loud fetch contract (PostgresAdapter raises).
PHP now raises DatabaseException from fetch()/fetchOne() like PostgresAdapter.
Python already fails loud (fetch/fetch_one let the driver error propagate);
Ruby already fails loud (execute_query re-raises). Pinned four-way so none can
regress. Mutation-proved: make PHP fetch swallow again -> the fail-loud case RED;
make Ruby execute_query swallow -> the Ruby fail-loud case RED.
The write-path fixture supplies the primary key EXPLICITLY on insert (a plain
INTEGER PK, not an auto-increment): ODBC has no reliable last-insert-id, and an
explicit key is exactly what exercises the PK-catalog introspection the update
path depends on. Affected-count assertions are Python-only (the @@IDENTITY
witness); the cross-language observable is row STATE read back, which is robust
across the four bindings.
Env contract (TINA4_TEST_ODBC_* convention): TINA4_TEST_ODBC_DSN is the
connection-string body (after odbc:///), e.g.
'DRIVER={PostgreSQL Unicode};SERVER=127.0.0.1;PORT=55432;DATABASE=tina4_odbc;
UID=tina4;PWD=tina4'. Unset -> the suite SKIPS cleanly (green) - a machine with
no ODBC is the skip case, not the design. TINA4_TEST_ODBC_AUTH_DSN is a
connection string to a PASSWORD-PROTECTED source with NO UID/PWD embedded (the
lab points it at PostgreSQL over its non-loopback IP, where pg_hba requires
scram), and TINA4_TEST_ODBC_USERNAME/_PASSWORD carry the creds - together they
prove the credentials are honoured (creds only as params -> connects) and that a
wrong password fails loud. The language ODBC bindings (pyodbc, PDO_ODBC,
ruby-odbc, node odbc) are the existing OPTIONAL ones - declared in the manifest
(pyproject `odbc` extra, Ruby Gemfile `:odbc` group, Node @tina4/orm
optionalDependencies); unixODBC + the driver are OS packages provisioned on the
lab, NOT framework deps. ZERO new runtime deps.
feature: 13 - ODBC provider (ODBC-DEC-01 provision a REAL ODBC source and run the shared write-path fixture through it; ODBC-DEC-02 the latent fixes it surfaces - the PK catalog stub, Python's @@IDENTITY/ignored credentials, Node's string-WHERE branch + executeMany owns-guard, PHP's swallow-to-empty fetch, and the Ruby connection-string connect + PHP factory gaps the real run exposed), against a real PostgreSQL over ODBC (psqlodbc)

invariants.rule: On a REAL ODBC source, the shared write path works end to end: a SELECT via db.fetch returns the inserted rows in order; db.insert(table, data) with an explicit primary key lands durably and reads back on a SECOND fresh connection; db.update(table, data) with the PK in data and NO explicit filter introspects the real primary key from the ODBC catalog and updates exactly that row (a table whose PK is not named `id` too); and a string-WHERE update (`id <= ?` + params) targets exactly the matching rows. Identical observable in all four (Python Database.insert/update -> ODBCAdapter; PHP Database::insert/update -> ODBCAdapter; Ruby Database#insert/update -> OdbcDriver; Node Database.insert/update -> OdbcAdapter).
invariants.why: ODBC-DEC-01 + ODBC-PK-STUB + ODBC-CONNECT: the CRUD path had never run against a real ODBC source, so provisioning one is what proved it - and caught that Ruby could not connect with a connection string (ODBC::Database.new -> SQLConnect wants a DSN NAME; now #drvconnect/SQLDriverConnect) and that PHP's factory could not instantiate odbc:/// at all (parse_url choked; now special-cased). The PK-keyed and non-id-PK updates are the ODBC-PK-STUB fix: get_columns/columns/getColumns hardcoded primary_key=false in all four, so the filterless-write guard could not introspect the key and threw; each adapter now reads the real PK (Python/Ruby/Node via SQLPrimaryKeys, PHP via INFORMATION_SCHEMA). The string-WHERE update is the ODBC-NODE-QUIRKS fix (Object.keys walked the string -> nonsense WHERE). Mutation-proved on the .99 lab: revert the PK read to false -> the PK-keyed + non-id cases throw the write-guard error RED (all four); revert Ruby #drvconnect -> every case RED (cannot connect); neuter Node's string branch -> the string-where case RED. No mocks.
cases: an insert round trips on a fresh connection
a pk keyed update with no filter works
a non id primary key update works
a string where update targets the right rows

invariants.rule: On a REAL ODBC source, a write with no filter is an error, not a full-table write: db.update(table, data) with neither an explicit filter nor the primary key in data RAISES rather than overwriting every row, and db.delete(table) with no filter RAISES rather than emptying the table (truncate is the explicit whole-table spelling). Feature 4's guard depends on the PK introspection that ODBC-PK-STUB fixed. Identical observable in all four.
invariants.why: The filterless-write guard (feature 4, P1) is only reachable on ODBC once get_columns reports a real primary_key (ODBC-PK-STUB) - otherwise primary_key() returns [] for every table and even a legitimate PK-keyed update is rejected. This pins that a genuinely UN-keyed filterless write is refused and the row/table is untouched. Proven with a positive (the guarded row keeps its value / the table keeps its row) alongside the raise. No mocks.

invariants.rule: On a REAL ODBC source, db.fetch and db.fetch_one on a genuinely broken query (a missing table) RAISE - they do NOT swallow the error to an empty result - while a good query on the same connection still returns its rows. Identical observable in all four (matching the SQL adapters and the Python master).
invariants.why: ODBC-FAILLOUD: PHP's ODBCAdapter fetch()/fetchOne() caught the driver error and returned []/null while execute() raised, so a real query error was hidden as 'no rows' - contrary to the fail-loud fetch contract PostgresAdapter holds. PHP now raises DatabaseException from fetch()/fetchOne() like PostgresAdapter (query() still records the error and returns [], the public fetch raises on it). Python and Ruby already fail loud (Python lets the pyodbc error propagate; Ruby's execute_query re-raises), pinned four-way so none can regress. Mutation-proved: make PHP fetch swallow again -> RED; make Ruby execute_query swallow -> RED. No mocks.
cases: a fetch on a bad query fails loud

invariants.rule: On a REAL password-protected ODBC source (no UID/PWD in the connection string), connecting with the correct username/password passed as SEPARATE parameters succeeds and a SELECT returns its row; connecting with a WRONG password RAISES. Identical observable in all four (Python/PHP/Ruby/Node each fold the separate creds into the connection string as UID/PWD).
invariants.why: ODBC-PY-QUIRKS (credentials): Python's connect() read only the raw connection string and IGNORED the username/password params, so an app that passed creds separately silently connected with none - fine against a trust source, rejected against an authenticating one. Python now appends UID/PWD; the same was wired through the Node factory (which also dropped separate creds for odbc). PHP already passes them to PDO and Ruby already appends them, pinned four-way. Proven against a real scram-authenticated PostgreSQL over ODBC (the lab's non-loopback IP, where pg_hba requires a password): creds only as params -> connects; wrong password -> the driver raises 'password authentication failed'. Mutation-proved (Python): drop the credential append -> the no-UID/PWD connection is rejected, the credentials case RED. No mocks.
cases: credentials passed as params are honoured

invariants.rule: On a REAL ODBC source, a batch insert (db.insert(table, [rows]), which routes through executeManyAsync) nested inside a caller's explicit transaction JOINS that transaction rather than committing it: a later db.rollback() undoes the batch AND every other write in the transaction, leaving the table empty. Node-specific (Node is the only adapter whose executeManyAsync managed its own commit).
invariants.why: ODBC-NODE-QUIRKS (owns-guard): executeManyAsync unconditionally started and committed a transaction, so nested inside a caller's transaction its commit() committed the OUTER transaction early and the caller's later rollback undid nothing. It now owns the transaction ONLY when not already inside one (owns = !inTransaction), mirroring pg/mysql/mssql and the Python master's owns_txn guard; insertAsync also now routes an array of rows through executeManyAsync so a batch insert reaches this path (it used to run Object.keys over the array -> a broken INSERT). Mutation-proved on the .99 lab: force owns=true -> the batch commits the outer transaction, 3 rows survive the rollback, RED. No mocks.
cases: a batch insert inside a transaction respects the callers rollback
